affordance_in_statement: Each veto is an unordered pair of distinct candidates who cannot be placed on the same committee. ... A trio is considered deadlocked if the trio is a subset of the incompatibility domain of each of its three members.
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal: the stated deadlocked-trio condition is intrinsically equivalent to finding a 3-clique in an undirected graph. Re-presenting it differently would require changing the task's core condition; removing the existence guarantee would also require specifying a valid no-solution output.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly constructs each incompatibility domain from graph neighbors and searches for a trio contained in all three domains.

common_affordance: The incompatibility-domain definition reduces the required obstruction to an undirected graph triangle: each of the three candidate pairs must be a recorded mutual veto.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: After adding each vertex itself to its bitmask, it tests common = da & db without removing the bits for a and b or requiring c > b. For every adjacent a,b, the intersection is therefore nonempty because it contains a and b, so it can output a non-distinct or invalid third candidate.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all survivors while preserving the task: their shared reduction is the intrinsic problem structure, not incidental wording. Any edit that prevents this reduction changes the deadlocked-trio condition itself.
